rows.title: From crime reporter to clown: Why clowning is having a moment
rows.standfirst: A crime reporter became a clown, leading us into a strange world of flops, reinvention and a scene that may or may not actually be booming.

rows.title: Which jobs are future-proofed?
rows.standfirst: With AI disrupting the workplace, is your job going to exist in ten years? The Bureau of Labor Statistics has just the handbook for that.

rows.title: Trump drinks Venezuela’s milkshake
rows.standfirst: One week ago, President Trump announced a deal that would give the “U.S. control of more than 65 BILLION BARRELS of proven Oil Reserves in Venezuela, at no cost to the American Taxpayer.”

rows.title: 4 things investigators learned about the dysfunction at Trump's Labor Department
rows.standfirst: A report from Labor Department investigators found former Labor Secretary Lori Chavez-DeRemer violated her own department's policy prohibiting harassment. She resigned in April.

rows.title: Pulling the SNAP lever + Why Gen Zers bet (invest?) differently
rows.standfirst: Changing SNAP eligibility actually can change consumption habits.

rows.title: Are job hoppers better at their jobs?
rows.standfirst: People with jobs are not always eager to leave them … but there are exceptions. Call them job hoppers. While many employers look down on this sort of professional promiscuity, new research suggests there are benefits to switching jobs frequently.

rows.title: The price of diesel hits a record high
rows.standfirst: The price of diesel has reached an all-time high, a result of the war in Iran and Ukraine's attacks on Russian refineries. That will matter across the supply chain.

rows.title: Fox News abruptly parts ways with scandal-tarred star Maria Bartiromo
rows.standfirst: Fox News abruptly announced it had cut ties with anchor Maria Bartiromo after more than a dozen years.

rows.title: Does Planet Money’s game pass the shelf test? We go undercover to find out
rows.standfirst: We go undercover at a big box store for an inside look at the secret shelf test the makers of Exploding Kittens use for their hit games.

rows.title: The IRS slashed its staff. One result? More taxes going uncollected
rows.standfirst: The IRS slashed its auditing staff last year — but the move may have backfired as tax collections from enforcement efforts plummeted, an Inspector General report shows.

rows.title: Chevron to expand in Venezuela, days after the U.S. and Venezuela strike oil deal
rows.standfirst: Chevron is the largest foreign oil operator in Venezuela. The deal will expand its footprint at a time of political and economic uncertainty for Venezuela.

rows.title: New lawsuits claim OpenAI execs put image ahead of safety in Canadian mass shooting
rows.standfirst: The suits say that recommendations to alert police about the alleged shooter were nixed by OpenAI's global affairs team, led by veteran political strategist Chris Lehane. OpenAI denies the claims.

rows.title: For a lot of Gen Z, gambling is investing
rows.standfirst: Why are more than half of Gen Zers using investment dollars for sports gambling? It’s been eight years since sports betting became widely legal. Today we look at its impact on a new generation of sports bettors and efforts to curb gambling’s more harmful effects.

rows.title: Love in the time of Palantir
rows.standfirst: To a lot of people, Palantir is a mystery — what does the company know, what data do they have, and (if they have it) what do they do with it all? We dig into that mystery and take you to a singles event to see if Big Data is good for Big Dating.

rows.title: 'It can outthink me': How a major manufacturer came to embrace AI
rows.standfirst: GE Appliances is leaning heavily into artificial intelligence to improve quality and efficiency on the factory floor.

rows.title: The powerful millionaires hiding in plain sight
rows.standfirst: They own car dealerships, law firms, dental practices, and restaurant chains. Collectively, these overlooked business owners hold far more wealth than the Forbes 400 — and wield considerable political power.

rows.title: A beautiful bill, Mamdani's market, and stock subscriptions
rows.standfirst: It’s time for another Indicator Quiz! For today’s quiz, we’re testing the Indicator knowledge of a brilliant mathematician. Will we stump his theoretician brain? Tune in and find out!

rows.title: Anthropic and OpenAI CEOs call for AI development to slow down, OpenAI to delay IPO
rows.standfirst: Dario Amodei and Sam Altman are the latest to urge caution amid fears the industry is racing too fast to build powerful AI while safety measures lag.

rows.title: The loan at the heart of a new foreclosure crisis
rows.standfirst: There is a new type of loan that is sweeping through the country right now. It’s advertised as a super quick and super easy way to get a mortgage to buy a home. In recent years, Wall Street has been funneling billions of dollars into these loans.

rows.title: Amid war and sanctions, many Iranians are losing their jobs and struggling to get by
rows.standfirst: Many Iranians lost their jobs because of the war and the U.S. blockade. Now some are even losing their backup jobs as sanctions tighten.

rows.title: Is Patagonia the new data center hub? + Harley-Davidson's role in the trade war
rows.standfirst: Why Patagonia might become a new data center hub

rows.title: US diesel prices soar past $6 a gallon, deepening strain for hauling everyday goods
rows.standfirst: Diesel prices in the U.S. has hit yet another record, soaring past $6 a gallon on average as Washington's war with Iran disrupts the world's flow of fuel

rows.title: From DOGE to "space lasers," Alex Gibney peels back the many layers of Elon Musk
rows.standfirst: In the Oscar-winning filmmaker's latest documentary, director Alex Gibney investigates the rise of Elon Musk and says what's behind Musk's success are distressing truths.

rows.title: The U.S.-Canada trade war is creating a headache for auto-parts makers
rows.standfirst: For decades, the U.S. and Canadian auto supply chains have been tightly woven together. The trade war is threatening to unravel a complex system.

rows.title: As data centers spread, not all U.S. housing markets react the same way
rows.standfirst: Realtors around the U.S. are being asked to explain how data centers could affect home values. But a new study shows there is no universal answer.

rows.title: Why gains by Iran-backed Houthis in Yemen could push gas prices even higher
rows.standfirst: A Houthi advance along Yemen's Red Sea coast could help push gas prices up even more as the Iran-backed group also launches attacks on Saudi Arabia's oil facilities.

rows.title: Bessent's yen bet, cold Argentine data centers set, and the summer box office net
rows.standfirst: This week’s indicators: Is The U.S. Treasury Department futzing with financial markets?; Is Patagonia’s pretty picturesque setting … for data centers?; Was the summer box office actually swell?

rows.title: Elon Musk threatens to sue over Gibney documentary's "space lasers" claim
rows.standfirst: The tech billionaire's attorney has put documentarian Alex Gibney and his production company on legal notice, claiming the Oscar-winning director defamed Musk in his nearly four-hour documentary.

rows.title: Are small town colleges going extinct?
rows.standfirst: Our favorite entry on the regional economy from the latest Beige Book reveals a troubling development in higher education.

rows.title: Fold the phone: Apple's new CEO unveils a foldable iPhone
rows.standfirst: New Apple CEO John Ternus announces the iPhone Duo, which folds like a passport and is the most radical iPhone design update in nearly 20 years.

rows.title: What’s at stake in President Trump’s showdown with the press?
rows.standfirst: President Trump's battle with the press has escalated. On Friday, he banned three outlets from the White House. Those outlets are suing the Trump administration over the ban. On Monday, the five networks that coordinate television coverage of the president agreed to suspend that coverage.

rows.title: Paramount makes concessions to salvage $111 billion Warner Bros. Discovery deal
rows.standfirst: Paramount's owners have made concessions to 12 Democratic state attorneys general to settle a lawsuit that endangered the media company's bid for its larger Hollywood rival, Warner Bros. Discovery.

rows.title: This farm raised thousands of pigs for slaughter. Now it's growing mushrooms instead
rows.standfirst: The U.S. gets nearly a third of its pork from Iowa. One family is making the switch from pigs to more sustainable specialty mushrooms and trying to show other pig farmers how they did it.

rows.title: How a national farm leader is dealing with record diesel prices
rows.standfirst: John Boyd Jr., president of the National Black Farmers Association, says soaring diesel costs are deepening a farm crisis as farmers face sharply higher fuel costs in the middle of harvest season.

rows.title: CNN, MS NOW and Politico sue Trump after being barred from White House
rows.standfirst: Reporters from CNN, MS NOW and Politico say they were prevented from entering the White House grounds after President Trump announced plans to ban all three outlets.

rows.title: How Hemp-THC businesses are bracing for a near total ban
rows.standfirst: Follow us to Tennessee where hemp farmers are already pivoting in the face of a state ban and soon, a looming federal ban on basically all THC-derived hemp products. Will Congress step in to save this $28 billion industry?

rows.title: Judge orders Fox to hand over hundreds of documents in shareholders' case
rows.standfirst: Fox Corp. must turn over hundreds of documents that could shed light on how founder Rupert Murdoch handled some of his media companies' biggest scandals.

rows.title: Ever wonder how the Fed's interest rate actually works? We've got answers
rows.standfirst: The Federal Reserve just raised interest rates this week for the first time this year. So how does it actually work? And what does it mean for the economy — and the rest of us? Here are some answers.

rows.title: Trump says he is banning CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House
rows.standfirst: The president chalked the ban up to what he called unfavorable coverage, and he threatened that bans on other media companies could be coming.

rows.title: The Domino’s Pizza Tracker Theory of Everything
rows.standfirst: Did a pizza restaurant’s humble status page change how we wait forever?

rows.title: When Trump and Xi meet they will discuss AI. 'Track Two' talks are already buzzing
rows.standfirst: An informal network of dialogues at think tanks and universities is bringing together experts from the U.S. and China to talk about the shared perils of AI — and possible paths forward.

rows.title: What expensive sulfur means for your dinner table
rows.standfirst: Oil supplies are falling, sulfur prices are threatening food costs, and we measure Lego against Hollywood

rows.title: Ms. Rachel has entered her album era, and she is so happy about it
rows.standfirst: Ms. Rachel has conquered YouTube, Netflix and the toy aisle. Now she's making an album, with real instruments, big feelings and her littlest listeners in mind.

rows.title: Warren Buffett steps down as Berkshire Hathaway chairman
rows.standfirst: Warren Buffett is stepping down as chairman of Berkshire Hathaway after serving in the role for more than 50 years. His son, Howard, will become Berkshire Hathaway's new chairman

rows.title: Could trees developed with gene-editing technology protect Florida's citrus industry?
rows.standfirst: A bacterial infection is wiping out Florida's citrus trees. Growers hope a rootstock developed with gene-editing technology could keep the disease at bay.

rows.title: Who’s gonna pay for your Social Security?
rows.standfirst: Very soon, Social Security may not have enough money to make full payments to retirees. Very soon. Like by 2032, just six years from now. So what are we gonna do about it?

rows.title: A startup wants to build a massive nuclear-powered data center on public land in Utah
rows.standfirst: Valar Atomics wants to place over 450 reactors on more than 9,500 acres in Utah to power a huge data center project.

rows.title: One year after the end of the EV tax credit, is the future still electric?
rows.standfirst: Congress got rid of a $7,500 federal tax credit for new electric vehicle buyers. One year later, are people still buying EVs?

rows.title: Is investing in sports worth it for universities?
rows.standfirst: Universities spend millions of dollars every year on their athletics programs. But does that investment pay off? Today, we interrogate the “Doug Flutie Effect.”

rows.title: How to hide your spending habits from retailers (so you don't get ripped off)
rows.standfirst: Companies have changed the way they price their products — and shoppers are getting deliberately overcharged. Here are steps you can take to ensure you are getting the best deal.

rows.title: Democrat Pete Buttigieg criticizes Trump's rollback of fuel-economy standards
rows.standfirst: The former transportation secretary says weaker fuel-economy standards could raise long-term costs for drivers and leave U.S. automakers further behind China.

rows.title: News organizations ask court to bar White House enforcement of access ban
rows.standfirst: Three news outlets that President Trump banished from White House grounds asked a federal court to block the ban until the case is resolved.

rows.title: How an obscure government code unlocks opportunity for businesses
rows.standfirst: What rhymes with "snakes" and helps the government classify economic activity? NAICS — or the North American Industry Classification System. These codes categorize every industry from artificial turf installation to zucchini farming. But they’re not exactly easy to get. Today we look at one business’ quest for a NAICS code and what makes them so valuable.

rows.title: The Trump administration weakens fuel efficiency standards for new cars
rows.standfirst: The Trump administration says easing these standards will make cars more affordable. Critics say it's not so simple and could be costly for the environment.

rows.title: What we know about the suspected U.K. terror plot. And, why the Gulf remains in limbo
rows.standfirst: What we know — and still don't — about the suspected terror plot near a U.K. air base. Trump rejects Iran's offer to pause fighting. And CNN prepares for new owners with ties to Trump.

rows.title: Smart-ring maker Oura delays its IPO citing market uncertainty
rows.standfirst: The leading smart ring manufacturer says the delay is "despite strong demand." It was betting its trove of health data would be a hit with Wall Street.

rows.title: How the rich make money by losing money
rows.standfirst: Decades ago, rich Americans used to pay taxes as high as 40% on their investments. Nowadays, an obscure investment strategy is helping them slash that figure toward … 0%. Today on the show, Bloomberg reporter Loukia Gyftopoulou, tells us about this generation’s “great American tax dodge,” and the “mad genius” behind it.

rows.title: Middlegarchs are the new Oligarchs
rows.standfirst: Wanna know who is really in the top 1%? And how they use their influence? It may not be who you think.

rows.title: Why this Pokémon set is dropping in value
rows.standfirst: How does one price a cemetery plot? Are they using dynamic pricing to figure it out? We tackle that question and many more in this week's Indicator newsletter.

rows.title: American farmers are hurting -- and worried about their futures
rows.standfirst: Farmers who grow soybeans, corn, cotton and other crops are facing another year of losses as soaring fuel and fertilizer costs offset higher revenues.
